brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L gap to our best prices and move to 30-day payment to free ₹10.63 L cash

priceAsk.summary: Match the prices Mars Plastics and Cincorp give us on the same items
priceAsk.target: ₹16.09 L annual saving by closing the gap on their rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.basis: Their 30 ml HDPE bottle is ₹1.65/NOS; Mars gives us ₹1.38/NOS (19.6% less). Their 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.90/NOS; Mars gives us ₹0.81/NOS (11.1% less). We already pay these lower prices to other suppliers for identical items — they must match.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.63 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we don't know their size, profit or cash position. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend may be small or large to them — we can't tell. Without that visibility we must lean on our own data: we have proof of better prices from Mars and Cincorp, and we have four strong alternate suppliers ready to quote. That gives us room to push firmly on price and terms, but we should also plan to qualify a second source in parallel so we're not guessing about their stability.

evidence.point: We pay ₹16.09 L more per year to Premier than the best prices we already get
Premier charges ₹1.65/NOS for the 30 ml HDPE bottle; Mars gives us ₹1.38/NOS — a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L annually on that SKU alone
Premier charges ₹0.90/NOS for the 28 mm PP cap; Mars gives us ₹0.81/NOS — an 11.1% gap costing ₹4.23 L per year
Market asks for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc — Premier's ₹0.90 is market-fair but there's room to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
evidence.figure: askBand ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict MARKET-FAIR; headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

evidence.point: Cutting payment terms from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L of our cash
We spend ₹1.29 Cr annually with Premier on rigid plastic packaging

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — strong and profitable, makes pails, containers and pharma packaging

alternates.name: Mars Plastics
alternates.why: Already our supplier for the same items at lower prices (₹1.38 vs ₹1.65 on 30 ml bottles, ₹0.81 vs ₹0.90 on caps) — a proven alternate

risks: Premier's finances aren't public, so we can't see if they're healthy or stretched — qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek in parallel so we have a backup if Premier pushes back hard or stumbles
If Premier refuses to match Mars's prices, we risk either paying the ₹16.09 L excess or scrambling to move volume mid-year — start the alternate RFQ now

Faster payment (30 days) is worth cash to us but only attractive to them if they're tight on cash; without knowing their position, lead with the price gap (which is hard proof) and offer the term shift as a trade if they resist
The market line for 28 mm caps says ₹0.90 is fair but there's headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at scale — if we consolidate more volume with one supplier we can push further than Mars's ₹0.81
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹16.09 lakh more each year than we pay Mars and Cincorp for the exact same bottles and caps — let's close that gap today.
